obligation.exact_statement: On the stationarily initialized D5 binary family, with rare frequency v in (0,1/4), w=(1-v)/3, t in [1/4,3/4], N>=3 and M=N-2, prove a finite-N statistical-versus-computational result for the complete actual single-query Route A representation Z_N(s)=(qtilde_N(s),r_N,mu_N(all four),query identity,retained terminal token residuals,raw-zero,length/type/constants), with no further raw-history access. Start from the admitted finite frontend and its explicit nominal matched-head error zeta_N, keeping every declared stream and its finite rational encoding. Establish a uniform explicit joint concentration bound for all eight empirical transition frequencies around pi_s p_t(y|s), preserving structural pair-chain zeros and endpoint dependence; a proposed bound is Pr(max|A_N-A_t|>h)<=16 exp(-M h^2/289). Transfer it to the full aggregate vector, and prove the correctly conditioned bound given the actual terminal query. For two D5 parameters t_±=1/2±Delta/2, 0<Delta<=1/2, give one common, admissible, observation-dependent post-aggregation error map (coordinate error <=delta on every q/r/mu copy, exact unchanged query/terminal/length channels) under which every decoder, including randomized ones, has a positive finite-N fixed-context and actual terminal-query conditional TV lower bound in an explicit nonempty sample/precision region. Account for the full finite encoding, including a common center encoding and all off-event outputs; no denominator-bit or residual bypass may be omitted. Derive the properly stationary-weighted actual average-risk consequence, not an independent-query substitution. In the same history, risk, bounded-encoding error model and explicit common resource envelope, prove a corresponding achievable upper bound using the admitted legal A or strong direct-correction implementation, showing how sampling error, implementation error and new aggregate perturbations enter and when the mechanism has a delta/v loss scale for fixed beta. Distinguish this scoped aggregate-channel necessity from an unrestricted Transformer lower bound, and from generic output quantization, deterministic rounding and independent random noise. Give valid constants or explicit asymptotic quantifiers and identify nonoptimal sample dependence; no population-only argument or deliberately slow inverse is allowed. This is one local finite-N prerequisite, not root closure.

Full-context and itemwise kernels, rare and uniform process families, and distinct error models remain separately scoped.
